To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a strategy to identify disease related QTL in mouse by undertaking single nucleotopic analysis.
we have developed a method of identifying candidate genes underlying the QTL mapped using the A/J and the B6 strains of the mouse.

the SNP analysis of the mouse lung tumour QTL region identified a candidate gene that is involved in tumour suppression and is a member of the p53 pathway, and the SNP analysis of mouse seizure QTL region identified two candidate genes, which may be involved in the regulation of the neuronal excitability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying candidate genes for disease related QTLS in mice.
identification of disease susceptibility genes in the mouse model.
the use of the mouse genome to identify the genetic basis of complex traits and diseases, with the ultimate goal being the development of new therapies and treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SNPs are a powerful tool for the identification of disease susceptibility genes.
SNP analysis can be undertaken to identify the candidate genes for disease susceptibility in mice.
SNP analysis of QTL is a useful approach to identifying the candidate genes for polygenic traits in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified 2.5 million SNPs between the A/J and C57BL6 strains of mice and have identified 3 candidate genes for lung cancer susceptibility.
the mouse genome sequence provides the basis for the identification of candidate genes for the QTLs that have been previously identified using classical genetic approaches.
we have identified 2,000 SNPs in the lung tumour susceptibility locus, 2,000 in the lung injury QTL, 3,000 in the disease resistance locus, and 1,500 in the seizure susceptibility locus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mouse genome sequences can be utilized to identify candidate genes for the disease related QTL.
the mouse genome sequences have made it possible for researchers to identify disease related candidate genes by SNP analysis of QTL mapped using A/J and B6129 F2 mice.
SNP analysis of QTL regions in the mouse genome can be used to identify candidate genes responsible for the QTL.
